title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
text: single inference method assumptions biases: correlation ignores compositionality, SparCC built compositional microbiome counts, SpiecEasi enforces sparsity partial correlations, WGCNA optimises scale-free topology. Different methods consequently disagree edges “real”. consensus network combines two single-method networks one keeps edges robustly supported across methods. Recent work microbiome research – CMiNet (Aghayeva et al. 2024) hybrid Bayesian / machine learning / network framework Chowdhury et al. (2024) – made case combining methods materially reduces method-specific bias sharpens biological interpretation. ggNetView::build_graph_from_consensus() takes list per-method adjacency matrices aggregates via one four strategies, three rank-fusion algorithms available rank-fusion route: output tbl_graph schema every build_graph_from_*() constructor, plugs directly ggNetView().

what: Step 1: Build per-method networks on the same data
title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
text: use package’s otu_rare_relative example data. keep vignette responsive restrict 40 abundant OTUs. construct three networks matrix using three different inference methods. exact downstream pipeline doesn’t matter consensus step – need adjacency matrix method. Note. real microbiome consensus workflow reach SparCC SpiecEasi capture compositionality partial correlation structure (available ggNetView via method = "SPARCC" method = "SpiecEasi"). use lighter correlation-family methods vignette builds quickly R CMD check. consensus API method-agnostic – requirement method produces square adjacency matrix row/column names matching across methods. Convert tbl_graph back adjacency matrix using get_graph_adjacency(): build_graph_from_consensus() aligns matrices common feature set automatically – see node_handling – three matrices need identical row/column orders.
code: data(otu_rare_relative) mat <- as.matrix(otu_rare_relative) mat <- mat[order(rowSums(mat), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(40)], ] dim(mat) #> [1] 40 18 # Method 1: Spearman correlation through psych::corr.test (no # compositionality assumption, baseline). g_cor <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat           = mat,   method        = "cor",   cor.method    = "spearman",   proc          = "BH",   r.threshold   = 0.4,   p.threshold   = 0.05,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis  # Method 2: WGCNA-style correlation (uses WGCNA::corAndPvalue + the # package's standard thresholding). Produces a different sparsity # pattern than plain correlation in practice. g_wgcna <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat           = mat,   method        = "WGCNA",   cor.method    = "spearman",   proc          = "BH",   r.threshold   = 0.4,   p.threshold   = 0.05,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis  # Method 3: Hmisc::rcorr -- another correlation engine with slightly # different missing-value handling and tie behaviour. g_hmisc <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat           = mat,   method        = "Hmisc",   cor.method    = "spearman",   r.threshold   = 0.4,   p.threshold   = 0.05,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis adj_cor   <- get_graph_adjacency(g_cor) adj_wgcna <- get_graph_adjacency(g_wgcna) adj_hmisc <- get_graph_adjacency(g_hmisc)  dim(adj_cor); dim(adj_wgcna); dim(adj_hmisc) #> [1] 17 17 #> [1] 17 17 #> [1] 9 9

title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
code: adj_list <- list(cor = adj_cor, wgcna = adj_wgcna, hmisc = adj_hmisc)  # Top-level strategies g_intersect <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "intersection",   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis  g_wavg <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "weighted_average",   threshold = 0.3,   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 3 we use the 3  modules for next analysis  g_majority <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "majority_vote",   binarize = "threshold",   binarize_threshold = 0.4,   min_methods = 2,   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 3 we use the 3  modules for next analysis  # Rank-fusion route, 3 algorithms g_borda <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "rank_fusion",   rank_fusion_algorithm = "borda",   threshold = 0.5,   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 3 we use the 3  modules for next analysis  g_rrf <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "rank_fusion",   rank_fusion_algorithm = "rrf",   threshold = 0.5,   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 3 we use the 3  modules for next analysis  g_rra <- build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list = adj_list,   method   = "rank_fusion",   rank_fusion_algorithm = "rra",   threshold = 0.5,   top_modules = 5,   seed = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis

title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
text: quick sanity check: many nodes edges strategy keep? strict strategies (intersection, majority_vote) tend produce sparser, conservative networks – edges robustly supported across methods survive. rank-fusion family typically yields denser networks ranks every pair lets user pick final cutoff via threshold.
code: summarise <- function(g, label) {   data.frame(     method = label,     n_nodes = igraph::gorder(g),     n_edges = igraph::gsize(g)   ) }  do.call(rbind, list(   summarise(g_intersect, "intersection"),   summarise(g_wavg,      "weighted_average"),   summarise(g_majority,  "majority_vote"),   summarise(g_borda,     "rank_fusion / borda"),   summarise(g_rrf,       "rank_fusion / rrf"),   summarise(g_rra,       "rank_fusion / rra") )) #>                method n_nodes n_edges #> 1        intersection       9       5 #> 2    weighted_average       9       9 #> 3       majority_vote       9       9 #> 4 rank_fusion / borda       9       9 #> 5   rank_fusion / rrf       9       9 #> 6   rank_fusion / rra       9       5

title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
text: starting point: Reach rank_fusion / rra want statistically justified consensus score notion “significantly supported uniform random ranking”. closest analogue CMiNet microbiome networks. Falls back Beta-order-statistic implementation optional RobustRankAggreg package installed. Reach rank_fusion / rrf robustness outlier ranks matters statistical interpretability. RRF parameter-free practice (k = 60 default information-retrieval convention). Reach rank_fusion / borda baseline – hyperparameters easiest explain. Reach intersection specifically want smallest, defensible set edges. Reach weighted_average one methods known reliable data want bias consensus toward (set weight higher weights). result strategy standard tbl_graph, every downstream analysis package – topological summaries (get_network_topology()), zi-pi role classification (ggnetview_zipi()), per-module subgraphs (get_subgraph()), full layout gallery – works without modification.

what: Importing networks built by external tools
title: Consensus Networks Across Multiple Inference Methods
text: build_graph_from_consensus() assume input matrices built ggNetView. Networks produced external R packages standalone tools (NetCoMi, CoNet, FlashWeave, CMiNet, …) can combined – long can express square numeric adjacency matrix row column names. Concretely: method-agnostic interface build_graph_from_adj_mat(), build_graph_from_df(), build_graph_from_node_edge(), build_graph_from_igraph(), build_graph_from_wgcna(), build_graph_from_stringdb() provide – extended accept multiple inputs .

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: vignette walks correlation-network family builders ggNetView. functions turn one numeric abundance / expression tables unified, module-annotated graph object can plotted directly ggNetView(). three main entry points : build_graph_from_mat() — single matrix, correlation network across rows (e.g. OTUs, genes, metabolites). build_graph_from_double_mat() — two matrices (two feature blocks) measured samples; edges represent cross-block correlations. build_graph_from_multi_mat() — generalizes double-matrix case three feature blocks. three return tidygraph object carrying correlation sign, edge weight, deterministic module assignment.

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: build_graph_from_mat() expects numeric matrix features rows samples columns. package ships otu_rare_relative, relative-abundance OTU table. fast example subset 60 abundant OTUs.
code: data(otu_rare_relative)  mat <- as.matrix(otu_rare_relative) row_sums <- rowSums(mat) mat <- mat[order(row_sums, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(60)], ]  graph_obj <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat           = mat,   method        = "cor",   cor.method    = "spearman",   proc          = "BH",   r.threshold   = 0.6,   p.threshold   = 0.05,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 11 we use the 11  modules for next analysis  graph_obj #> # A tbl_graph: 39 nodes and 67 edges #> # #> # An undirected simple graph with 10 components #> # #> # Node Data: 39 × 7 (active) #>    name   modularity modularity2 modularity3 Modularity Degree Strength #>    <chr>  <fct>      <ord>       <chr>       <ord>       <dbl>    <dbl> #>  1 ASV_41 1          1           1           1              11     8.80 #>  2 ASV_39 1          1           1           1              11     8.65 #>  3 ASV_10 1          1           1           1              10     7.73 #>  4 ASV_6  1          1           1           1               9     7.21 #>  5 ASV_2  1          1           1           1               8     6.50 #>  6 ASV_17 1          1           1           1               8     6.44 #>  7 ASV_44 1          1           1           1               8     6.15 #>  8 ASV_56 1          1           1           1               7     5.07 #>  9 ASV_24 1          1           1           1               4     2.90 #> 10 ASV_62 1          1           1           1               4     2.92 #> # ℹ 29 more rows #> # #> # Edge Data: 67 × 5 #>    from    to weight correlation corr_direction #>   <int> <int>  <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>          #> 1    15    17  0.750       0.750 Positive       #> 2    12    15  0.730       0.730 Positive       #> 3     4     5  0.783       0.783 Positive       #> # ℹ 64 more rows

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: Passing node annotation table merges metadata onto vertices. first column annotation must match feature names. Downstream plots can now colour facet taxonomy column (Phylum, Class, …).
code: data(tax_tab)  annot <- tax_tab[tax_tab$OTUID %in% rownames(mat), ] graph_obj_annot <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat             = mat,   method          = "cor",   cor.method      = "spearman",   proc            = "BH",   r.threshold     = 0.6,   p.threshold     = 0.05,   module.method   = "Fast_greedy",   node_annotation = annot,   seed            = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 11 we use the 11  modules for next analysis

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: ggNetView() single plotting entry point. Edge colour follows correlation sign automatically; node fill can driven Modularity column attached via node_annotation.  Swap layouts changing layout string — every layout uses supplied seed figures reproducible.
code: ggNetView(   graph_obj_annot,   layout    = "fr",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 7),   node_fill   = "Modularity",   module_label     = FALSE ) ggNetView(   graph_obj_annot,   layout    = "circle",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 7),   node_fill   = "Modularity" )

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: Use build_graph_from_double_mat() two feature blocks measured samples want edges cross two blocks (e.g. bacteria ↔︎ fungi, microbes ↔︎ metabolites). matrices must share sample column names. returned graph behaves identically single-matrix case, ggNetView() call works:  bipartite-style rendering, swap layout = "fr" "bipartite" supply block assignment via node_annotation.
code: data(BASV_tab) data(FASV_tab)  mat_b <- as.matrix(BASV_tab) mat_f <- as.matrix(FASV_tab)  double_obj <- build_graph_from_double_mat(   mat1          = mat_b,   mat2          = mat_f,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 4 we use the 4  modules for next analysis  double_obj #> # A tbl_graph: 100 nodes and 2500 edges #> # #> # An undirected simple graph with 1 component #> # #> # Node Data: 100 × 8 (active) #>    name   modularity modularity2 modularity3 Modularity Degree Segree Strength #>    <chr>  <fct>      <fct>       <chr>       <fct>       <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl> #>  1 BASV3  1          1           1           1              50     50    12.5  #>  2 BASV6  1          1           1           1              50     50     9.86 #>  3 BASV8  1          1           1           1              50     50    13.7  #>  4 BASV13 1          1           1           1              50     50    13.6  #>  5 BASV17 1          1           1           1              50     50    14.1  #>  6 BASV19 1          1           1           1              50     50    13.2  #>  7 BASV25 1          1           1           1              50     50    12.5  #>  8 BASV26 1          1           1           1              50     50    12.9  #>  9 BASV27 1          1           1           1              50     50    14.2  #> 10 BASV31 1          1           1           1              50     50    14.8  #> # ℹ 90 more rows #> # #> # Edge Data: 2,500 × 5 #>    from    to weight correlation corr_direction #>   <int> <int>  <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>          #> 1    15    57  0.338      -0.338 Negative       #> 2    57    90  0.648       0.648 Positive       #> 3    16    57  0.162       0.162 Positive       #> # ℹ 2,497 more rows ggNetView(   double_obj,   layout    = "fr",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 6),   node_fill   = "Modularity",   module_label     = FALSE )

text: three builders return tidygraph object, node- edge-level tibbles directly accessible via get_graph_nodes() get_info_from_graph(): Every node carries: Modularity — top-k module label (Others bucket many small modules) Degree, Strength — degree weighted degree column merged node_annotation Every edge carries: weight — absolute correlation correlation — signed correlation corr_direction — "Positive" / "Negative"
code: head(get_graph_nodes(graph_obj)) #>     name modularity modularity2 modularity3 Modularity Degree Strength #> 1 ASV_41          1           1           1          1     11 8.800914 #> 2 ASV_39          1           1           1          1     11 8.653297 #> 3 ASV_10          1           1           1          1     10 7.729325 #> 4  ASV_6          1           1           1          1      9 7.212516 #> 5  ASV_2          1           1           1          1      8 6.495174 #> 6 ASV_17          1           1           1          1      8 6.444404 lapply(get_info_from_graph(graph_obj), head, 3) #> $node_info #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   name   Modularity Degree Strength #>   <chr>  <ord>       <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 ASV_41 1              11     8.80 #> 2 ASV_39 1              11     8.65 #> 3 ASV_10 1              10     7.73 #>  #> $edge_info #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   from   to     weight correlation corr_direction #>   <chr>  <chr>   <dbl>       <dbl> <chr>          #> 1 ASV_1  ASV_21  0.750       0.750 Positive       #> 2 ASV_34 ASV_1   0.730       0.730 Positive       #> 3 ASV_6  ASV_2   0.783       0.783 Positive

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: get_network_topology() computes global network metrics plus bootstrap-based robustness summary. accepts either pre-built graph object raw matrix — latter case builder re-run internally r.threshold / p.threshold / method combination applied. return value list least two elements: topology — one row global metrics (number nodes / edges, average degree, clustering coefficient, modularity, …). robustness — bootstrap summary network-level metrics behave random node removal, used estimate stability. sample × feature designs (e.g. microbiome studies many samples) use get_sample_subgraph_topology() _parallel variant compute metrics per-sample.
code: topo <- get_network_topology(graph_obj = graph_obj, bootstrap = 20) names(topo) #> [1] "topology"   "Robustness" head(topo$topology) #> # A tibble: 6 × 3 #>   Topology Target_network Random_nerwork #>   <chr>             <dbl>          <dbl> #> 1 Node            39             39      #> 2 Edge            67             67      #> 3 Degree           3.44           3.44   #> 4 Distance         1.27           2.95   #> 5 Diameter         3.04           6.45   #> 6 Density          0.0904         0.0904

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: ggnetview_zipi() classifies every node within-module connectivity (Zi) among-module participation coefficient (Pi). default thresholds (Zi = 2.5, Pi = 0.62) Guimerà & Amaral (2005) split nodes four roles: Peripherals — low Zi, low Pi Connectors — low Zi, high Pi Module hubs — high Zi, low Pi Network hubs — high Zi, high Pi takes node table adjacency matrix — accessible directly ggNetView graph object: plot element result ready--render Zi-Pi scatter plot four quadrants shaded:
code: nodes_tbl <- get_graph_nodes(graph_obj) adj_mat   <- get_graph_adjacency(graph_obj)  zipi <- ggnetview_zipi(   nodes_bulk     = nodes_tbl,   z_bulk_mat     = adj_mat,   modularity_col = "Modularity",   degree_col     = "Degree" )  head(zipi$data[, c("name", "within_module_connectivities",                    "among_module_connectivities", "type")]) #>     name within_module_connectivities among_module_connectivities        type #> 1 ASV_41                   1.29567300                   0.1652893 Peripherals #> 2 ASV_39                   1.29567300                   0.1652893 Peripherals #> 3 ASV_10                   0.87648467                   0.1800000 Peripherals #> 4  ASV_6                   0.45729635                   0.1975309 Peripherals #> 5  ASV_2                   0.03810803                   0.2187500 Peripherals #> 6 ASV_17                   0.03810803                   0.2187500 Peripherals zipi$plot

title: Correlation-based Network Pipelines
text: Layout gallery: pass layout = "..." string accepted ggNetView() — 30+ deterministic layouts, including "circular_modules_petal", "cross_quadripartite_gephi", "star_concentric". Module comparison across networks: build named list graph objects feed get_network_topology(graph_obj_list = ...) get per-network metrics one call; use ggnetview_modularity_heatmaps() visualise module composition side--side. RMT thresholding: ggNetView_RMT() picks data-driven correlation threshold using random matrix theory — useful want hand-tune r.threshold. Multi-network rendering: ggNetView_multi() / ggNetView_multi_link() plot several networks shared coordinate system aligned modules.

title: Introduction to ggNetView
text: ggNetView provides reproducible, deterministic framework analyzing visualizing biological, ecological, microbial association networks. package combines: family build_graph_from_*() functions turn adjacency matrices, correlation matrices, edge lists, igraph objects unified tidygraph-backed network object module annotations; topology utilities (get_network_topology(), get_info_from_graph(), get_graph_nodes()) node- network-level metrics; large collection deterministic layout generators (dispatched ggNetView() via layout argument); ggplot2-compatible plotting function ggNetView() publication-quality figures. vignette walks end--end workflow: loading bundled example, building graph object, extracting information, rendering plot.

title: Introduction to ggNetView
text: ggNetView ships several example datasets. use ppi_example, small protein–protein interaction network 100 nodes 200 edges. build_graph_from_igraph() detects communities (Fast-greedy algorithm), simplifies multi-edges self-loops, attaches node-level attributes (Modularity, Degree, Strength) downstream plotting.

text: ggNetView() function main entry point plotting. layout argument selects one deterministic layout generators shipped package. render network Fruchterman–Reingold layout color nodes module. title: Layout Gallery
text: reuse bundled OTU data build small, well-connected network clear modules. small helper keep gallery code concise:
code: data(otu_rare_relative) data(tax_tab)  mat <- as.matrix(otu_rare_relative) mat <- mat[order(rowSums(mat), decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(80)], ] annot <- tax_tab[tax_tab$OTUID %in% rownames(mat), ]  g <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat             = mat,   method          = "cor",   cor.method      = "spearman",   proc            = "BH",   r.threshold     = 0.6,   p.threshold     = 0.05,   module.method   = "Fast_greedy",   node_annotation = annot,   seed            = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 11 we use the 11  modules for next analysis show_layout <- function(layout_name, ...) {   ggNetView(     g,     layout    = layout_name,     seed      = 1,     node_size_range = c(2, 6),     node_fill   = "Modularity",     module_label     = FALSE,     ...   ) +     ggplot2::ggtitle(layout_name) }

title: Layout Gallery
text: Multipartite layouts separate nodes two spatially distinct groups. Use nodes categorical block attribute (e.g. bacteria vs. fungi, different experimental groups). layout_module parameter controls modules arranged: "random" – modules distributed freely "adjacent" – modules positioned close together "order" – modules follow block order (required multipartite) layouts require number modules matches expected block count (e.g. bipartite needs exactly 2, tripartite needs 3).
code: # Bipartite (2-block) show_layout("bipartite_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("bipartite_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order")  # Tripartite (3-block) show_layout("tripartite_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("tripartite_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("tripartite_equal_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order")  # Quadripartite (4-block) show_layout("quadripartite_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("quadripartite_equal_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("cross_quadripartite_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("cross_quadripartite_equal_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order")  # Pentapartite (5-block) show_layout("pentapartite_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order") show_layout("pentapartite_equal_gephi_layout", layout_module = "order")

title: Virtual Perturbation Analysis

Interpretation caveat. Correlation / co-occurrence networks encode association, causation, edge direction. structural analysis (type 1) depends topology robust. influence (type 2) press (type 3) analyses borrow ideas dynamical ecology use correlations proxies interaction strengths – read output qualitative scenarios, quantitative predictions.

title: Virtual Perturbation Analysis
text: get_network_perturbation() removes nodes step step recomputes panel connectivity metrics removal. headline metric LCC_fraction – size largest connected component relative original network – single-number summary Schneider R-index (area LCC curve; higher = robust). informative comparison random failure targeted attack (removing -connected nodes first): lower R-index targeted attack classic signature scale-free-like network: tolerates random loss fragile deliberate removal hubs. Overlay curves companion plotting helper:  can target centrality ("degree", "strength", "betweenness", "closeness", "eigenvector", "ivi"), curve table also carries Natural_connectivity, Efficiency, Modularity , can plot different metric:
code: rnd <- get_network_perturbation(   g, strategy = "random", bootstrap = 30, seed = 1, plot = FALSE )  tgt <- get_network_perturbation(   g, strategy = "targeted", centrality = "degree", plot = FALSE )  rbind(rnd$robustness_index, tgt$robustness_index) #>   strategy   R_index #> 1   random 0.2347257 #> 2 targeted 0.1453634 ggnetview_perturbation_curve(rbind(rnd$curve, tgt$curve)) #> Warning: Removed 21 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`). ggnetview_perturbation_curve(tgt$curve, metric = "Natural_connectivity")

title: Virtual Perturbation Analysis
text: get_node_influence() injects virtual perturbation one source nodes lets diffuse along (signed) weighted edges, returning per-node Influence score. Positive vs negative values distinguish neighbours move vs source. score stored node column, can map onto network figure. ggNetView()’s node_fill aesthetic uses discrete scale, bin signed influence small categorical column first:
code: hub <- get_graph_nodes(g) |>   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(Degree)) |>   dplyr::pull(name) |>   head(1)  g_infl <- get_node_influence(g, source = hub)  get_graph_nodes(g_infl) |>   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(abs(Influence))) |>   dplyr::select(name, Modularity, Degree, Influence) |>   head(8) #>     name Modularity Degree   Influence #> 1 ASV_41          2     17  0.07055545 #> 2  ASV_2          1     16  0.06542196 #> 3 ASV_39          2     17  0.06525645 #> 4 ASV_73          2     14  0.06224600 #> 5 ASV_66          1     15 -0.05980907 #> 6 ASV_44          1     13  0.05866859 #> 7  ASV_6          2     14  0.05639881 #> 8 ASV_17          2     13  0.05530194 g_infl <- g_infl |>   tidygraph::activate(nodes) |>   tidygraph::mutate(Influence_class = dplyr::case_when(     Influence > 0 ~ "Co-moves (+)",     Influence < 0 ~ "Counter-moves (-)",     TRUE          ~ "Unreached"   ))  ggNetView(g_infl, layout = "fr", node_fill = "Influence_class")

title: Virtual Perturbation Analysis
text: press_perturbation() treats signed correlation matrix proxy community matrix \(\), adds negative self-regulation diagonal, inverts get net-effect matrix \(N = -^{-1}\). Entry \(N_{ij}\) long-run net response species \(\) species \(j\) held sustained pressure. diagonal chosen automatically guarantee dynamically stable matrix, stability reported: Query consequences continuously pressing hub species – nodes largest absolute response ones affected: positive net_response means species tends increase source boosted (decrease suppressed); negative value means opposite.
code: pp <- press_perturbation(g)  c(stable = pp$stable,   eigen_real_max = round(pp$eigen_real_max, 3),   self_regulation = round(pp$self_regulation, 3)) #>          stable  eigen_real_max self_regulation  #>           1.000          -1.000         -11.103 pp_hub <- press_perturbation(g, source = hub) head(pp_hub$response, 8) #>      name net_response #> 1  ASV_10   0.16032271 #> 15 ASV_41   0.08101214 #> 16 ASV_39   0.07794091 #> 2   ASV_2   0.07336664 #> 18 ASV_73   0.07210790 #> 17  ASV_6   0.07207952 #> 19 ASV_17   0.06951217 #> 20 ASV_60   0.06885498

title: Network Topology and Keystone Analysis
text: Zi-Pi framework (Guimera & Amaral, 2005) classifies node two metrics: Zi (within-module connectivity) – well connected node within module. Pi (participation coefficient) – much node connects modules. Default thresholds (Zi = 2.5, Pi = 0.62) divide nodes four roles:

text: Zi-Pi scatter plot. Quadrants identify node roles.
code: zipi$plot

title: Network Topology and Keystone Analysis
text: Peripherals (nodes) – loosely connected within across modules. follow community structure passively. Module hubs – highly connected within module bridging others. Removal destabilises module. Connectors – bridge nodes linking different modules. Important network-wide information flow. Network hubs – intra- inter-module hubs. critical nodes; candidates keystone species genes.

title: Node-Importance Analysis: Multiple Centralities and IVI
text: Degree simplest measure node importance, ’s network analyses lead – including per-node Degree Strength columns every build_graph_from_*() constructor ggNetView already attaches. degree counts node’s immediate neighbours; doesn’t tell whether neighbours sit shortest paths distant communities (betweenness), whether node “central” global topology (closeness, eigenvector), whether functions bridge modules (Zi-Pi). defensible node-importance analysis usually want several complementary perspectives, plus integrative score combines . ggNetView exposes node-importance functionality three levels:

what: Step 2: Different centralities highlight different nodes
title: Node-Importance Analysis: Multiple Centralities and IVI
text: common observation network biology single centrality captures “important” nodes – node can high-degree hub without many shortest paths, vice versa. can quantify disagreement: two centralities perfect agreement pairwise overlap 10; disagreed completely 0. Real microbiome / gene networks usually fall somewhere , gap exactly single-metric importance ranking misses.
code: node_df <- obj_aug %>%   tidygraph::activate(nodes) %>%   tidygraph::as_tibble()  top_n <- 10 top_lists <- list(   Degree      = node_df$name[order(-node_df$Degree)][seq_len(top_n)],   Betweenness = node_df$name[order(-node_df$Betweenness)][seq_len(top_n)],   PageRank    = node_df$name[order(-node_df$PageRank)][seq_len(top_n)],   Eigenvector = node_df$name[order(-node_df$Eigenvector)][seq_len(top_n)] )  # Pairwise overlap between top-10 lists. pairs <- utils::combn(names(top_lists), 2, simplify = FALSE) do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs, function(pair) {   data.frame(     a = pair[1L],     b = pair[2L],     overlap_top10 = length(intersect(top_lists[[pair[1L]]],                                      top_lists[[pair[2L]]]))   ) })) #>             a           b overlap_top10 #> 1      Degree Betweenness             6 #> 2      Degree    PageRank             6 #> 3      Degree Eigenvector             9 #> 4 Betweenness    PageRank             8 #> 5 Betweenness Eigenvector             5 #> 6    PageRank Eigenvector             5

what: Picking a defensible threshold for “significantly influential”
title: Node-Importance Analysis: Multiple Centralities and IVI
text: Default get_node_ivi() uses influential::ivi(scale = "range"), normalises IVI [1, 100] – great inspecting full spread node influences within one network. Two scaling modes support different downstream questions: scale = "z-scale" standardises IVI z-score. Use comparing influence across multiple networks (e.g. gut vs soil microbiome), want numeric threshold backed one-sided 0.05 cutoff – IVI paper suggests z > 1.645. scale = "none" returns raw IVI scores untouched. Larger IVI always means influential, ranking dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(IVI)) works identically across three scaling choices.
code: obj_z <- get_node_ivi(obj_aug, scale = "z-scale") obj_z %>%   tidygraph::activate(nodes) %>%   tidygraph::as_tibble() %>%   dplyr::filter(IVI > 1.645) %>%   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(IVI)) %>%   dplyr::select(name, Modularity, Degree, IVI) #> # A tibble: 1 × 4 #>   name   Modularity Degree   IVI #>   <chr>  <ord>       <dbl> <dbl> #> 1 ASV_50 3               9  4.64

what: Step 4 (optional): Map IVI onto a network plot
title: Node-Importance Analysis: Multiple Centralities and IVI
text: also want network plot IVI visual aesthetic, can pass IVI-augmented graph ggNetView(). Two notes: ggNetView() discrete-fill plotter – node_fill argument maps ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(), expects factor / character column, raw numeric. Easiest fix: bin IVI small ordered factor first (quartiles usually informative), pass bin column node_fill. Network coloured IVI quartile; warmer = influential. recipe works continuous centrality column (Betweenness, PageRank, Eigenvector, …): wrap cut() produce ordered factor, pass factor node_fill.
code: obj_plot <- obj_aug %>%   tidygraph::activate(nodes) %>%   tidygraph::mutate(     IVI_bin = cut(       IVI,       breaks = stats::quantile(IVI, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25), na.rm = TRUE),       labels = c("Q1 (low)", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4 (high)"),       include.lowest = TRUE,       ordered_result = TRUE     )   )  ggNetView(   obj_plot,   layout    = "fr",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 8),   node_fill   = "IVI_bin",   module_label     = FALSE )

title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
text: Scale-free topology fit versus soft-thresholding power. Choose lowest power model fit (\(R^2\)) exceeds 0.85.
code: # Force WGCNA into single-threaded mode before calling # `pickSoftThreshold()`. WGCNA spins up an internal foreach/parallel # cluster by default, which is fragile inside vignette / R CMD check # environments (and intermittently dies with # "Error in summary.connection(connection) : invalid connection"). # Single-threaded is slower but deterministic and side-effect-free, # which is exactly what we want for reproducible documentation. Users # can re-enable parallelism for production work via # `WGCNA::allowWGCNAThreads()` or `WGCNA::enableWGCNAThreads()`. WGCNA::disableWGCNAThreads()  powers <- c(seq(1, 10, by = 1), seq(12, 30, by = 2)) sft <- WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(   expr_mat,   powerVector  = powers,   networkType  = "signed",   verbose      = 0 ) #>    Power SFT.R.sq  slope truncated.R.sq mean.k. median.k. max.k. #> 1      1  0.64600  8.260         0.7460  40.200   40.2000  44.30 #> 2      2  0.17700  1.850         0.2240  22.500   21.8000 5.2600  13.00 #> 6      6  0.46400 -1.250         0.4430   4.570    3.5900  11.10 #> 7      7  0.51400 -1.290         0.5750   3.490    2.5400   9.73 #> 8      8  0.56400 -1.180         0.6800   2.750    1.8200   8.72 #> 9      9  0.51600 -1.110         0.6140   2.230    1.3500   7.91 #> 10    10  0.59900 -1.140         0.6930   1.850    1.0400   7.24 #> 11    12  0.70000 -1.130         0.7580   1.340    0.6550   6.19 #> 12    14  0.02260 -0.940        -0.0480   1.020    0.4450   5.38 #> 13    16  0.75600 -1.060         0.7700   0.808    0.2980   4.73 #> 14    18  0.80400 -1.070         0.7940   0.654    0.2060   4.19 #> 15    20  0.07210 -1.410        -0.0909   0.538    0.1460   3.74 #> 16    22  0.87800 -1.000         0.8720   0.450    0.1070   3.36 #> 17    24  0.95000 -0.961 (signed R^2)",      main = "Scale independence",      type = "n") text(sft$fitIndices[, 1],      -sign(sft$fitIndices[, 3]) * sft$fitIndices[, 2],      labels = powers, col = "red") abline(h = 0.85, col = "red") picked_power <- sft$powerEstimate if (is.na(picked_power)) picked_power <- 6 message("Using soft-thresholding power: ", picked_power) #> Using soft-thresholding power: 22

what: Step 3: Build TOM and detect modules
title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
code: adjacency <- WGCNA::adjacency(   expr_mat,   power       = picked_power,   type        = "signed",   corFnc      = "cor",   corOptions  = list(method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs") )  TOM <- WGCNA::TOMsimilarity(adjacency, TOMType = "signed") #> ..connectivity.. #> ..matrix multiplication (system BLAS).. #> ..normalization.. #> ..done. dissTOM <- 1 - TOM  gene_tree <- hclust(as.dist(dissTOM), method = "average")  dynamic_mods <- dynamicTreeCut::cutreeDynamic(   dendro    = gene_tree,   distM     = dissTOM,   deepSplit = 2,   minClusterSize = 5 ) #>  ..cutHeight not given, setting it to 0.997  ===>  99% of the (truncated) height range in dendro. #>  ..done.  module_colors <- WGCNA::labels2colors(dynamic_mods) module_df <- data.frame(   ID     = colnames(expr_mat),   Module = module_colors,   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) head(module_df) #>      ID    Module #> 1 ASV_1      grey #> 2 ASV_2 turquoise #> 3 ASV_3      grey #> 4 ASV_4      grey #> 5 ASV_8      grey #> 6 ASV_6 turquoise

what: Step 4: Convert TOM to edge list
title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
text: trans_TOM_in_WGCNA() converts dense TOM matrix long-format edge list (, , weight). Use threshold argument keep strongest edges:
code: # `trans_TOM_in_WGCNA()` uses `colnames(mat)` as node IDs, so `mat` must # be in the same orientation as the input to `WGCNA::adjacency()`: # samples in rows, features (genes/OTUs) in columns. `expr_mat` is # already in that shape (we transposed once at Step 1), so pass it # straight in -- transposing again would swap node IDs to sample IDs and # fail the dimension check inside trans_TOM_in_WGCNA(). edge_df <- trans_TOM_in_WGCNA(   TOM       = TOM,   mat       = expr_mat,   threshold = 0.1 ) head(edge_df) #>     from     to    weight #> 1  ASV_2  ASV_6 0.1484648 #> 2  ASV_2 ASV_10 0.1511034 #> 3  ASV_6 ASV_10 0.1168046 #> 4  ASV_2 ASV_17 0.1204909 #> 5  ASV_6 ASV_17 0.4528145 #> 6 ASV_10 ASV_17 0.1158161 dim(edge_df) #> [1] 59  3

title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
text: Full WGCNA pipeline – Fruchterman-Reingold layout. Try different layouts highlight module structure: Circular module layout groups nodes WGCNA module.
code: ggNetView(   graph_full,   layout    = "fr",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 7),   node_fill   = "Modularity",   module_label     = FALSE ) # Note the `_layout` suffix: the petal-style layout functions are named # `create_layout_circular_modules_petal_layout()` (and the *2 variant), # whereas other layouts like `fr` / `gephi` / `kk` use the bare name. The # `layout` argument is concatenated to `create_layout_` to look up the # function, so it must include the suffix here. ggNetView(   graph_full,   layout    = "circular_modules_petal_layout",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 6),   node_fill   = "Modularity",   module_label     = FALSE )

title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
text: unsure r.threshold use, Random Matrix Theory (RMT) can pick one automatically. ggNetView_RMT() scans range thresholds selects one whose nearest-neighbour spacing distribution best fits Poisson (non-random) model. Feed chosen threshold back builder: Network built RMT-selected threshold.
code: rmt_res <- ggNetView_RMT(   mat     = mat,   method  = "WGCNA",   cor.method = "spearman",   nr_thresholds = 31,   verbose = FALSE,   seed    = 1 ) #> Warning in ggNetView_RMT(mat = mat, method = "WGCNA", cor.method = "spearman", #> : Matrix is relatively small (<100): RMT statistics may be unstable.  message("RMT chosen threshold: ", round(rmt_res$chosen_threshold, 4)) #> RMT chosen threshold: 0.6798 graph_rmt <- build_graph_from_mat(   mat           = mat,   method        = "WGCNA",   cor.method    = "spearman",   proc          = "BH",   r.threshold   = rmt_res$chosen_threshold,   p.threshold   = 0.05,   module.method = "Fast_greedy",   seed          = 1 ) #> The max module in network is 10 we use the 10  modules for next analysis ggNetView(   graph_rmt,   layout    = "fr",   seed      = 1,   node_size_range = c(2, 7),   node_fill   = "Modularity",   module_label     = FALSE )

title: WGCNA Network Pipeline
text: scores element contains per-threshold diagnostics. quick plot helps verify choice: KS p-value (higher = Poisson-like) across thresholds.
code: scores <- rmt_res$scores plot(scores$threshold, scores$ks_p,      type = "b", pch = 16,      xlab = "Correlation threshold",      ylab = "KS p-value (Exponential fit)",      main = "RMT threshold scan") abline(v = rmt_res$chosen_threshold, lty = 2, col = "red")

code: # ---- Multi-network "linked" view (no per-group scale normalisation) ---- # `ggNetView_multi_link()` builds ONE network per group (defined by `group_info`), # lays each one out independently, and places all sub-networks on a circular # anchor frame so that cross-group edges/relationships can be visually compared. out1 <- ggNetView_multi_link(   mat              = otu_rare_relative, # variables x samples abundance matrix   group_info       = otu_sample,        # sample metadata; defines how samples are split into groups   transfrom.method = "none",            # pre-correlation transform on `mat`; "none" = keep as-is   r.threshold      = 0.7,               # |r| cutoff for keeping an edge   p.threshold      = 0.05,              # adjusted p-value cutoff   method           = "WGCNA",           # correlation backend: WGCNA::corAndPvalue   cor.method       = "pearson",         # Pearson correlation   proc             = "BH",              # multiple-testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg)   module.method    = "Fast_greedy",     # community detection per sub-network   layout_module    = "adjacent",        # neighbouring modules placed close together   center           = T,                 # pull a node toward the centre of each sub-layout   top_modules      = 15,                # keep top-15 modules per sub-network; rest -> "Others"   layout           = "gephi",           # global node-positioning algorithm per sub-network   shrink           = 0.5,               # shrink each sub-network inward (smaller = more compact)   scale            = F,                 # do NOT normalise each group to a common scale -> sub-networks keep their native size differences   node_jitter      = T,                 # jitter node positions slightly to reduce overlap   node_jitter_sd   = 0.3,               # SD of the jitter (bigger -> more spread)   anchor_dist      = 30,                 # distance between groups on the outer anchor circle   seed             = 1115,              # fix RNG for reproducibility   orientation      = "up",              # frame orientation; one of "up"/"down"/"left"/"right"   angle            = 0                  # additional rotation angle (degrees) ) #> Scale for size is already present. #> Adding another scale for size, which will replace the existing scale. #> Scale for size is already present. #> Adding another scale for size, which will replace the existing scale.  p1 <- out1[["p"]]   # code: # ---- RMT threshold scan #1: WGCNA correlation backend ---- # `ggNetView_RMT()` scans a series of candidate |r| thresholds, builds the # thresholded correlation matrix at each, computes its eigenvalue spacing # distribution (NNSD), and picks the threshold at which the NNSD transitions # from Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (signal + noise) to Poisson (noise-free, # modular network) — this is the RMT-recommended cutoff. out <- ggNetView_RMT(   mat              = otu_rare_relative, # input matrix (variables x samples)   transfrom.method = "none",            # already relative-abundance, no extra transform   method           = "WGCNA",           # use WGCNA::corAndPvalue for correlation   cor.method       = "pearson",         # Pearson correlation   unfold.method    = "gaussian",        # Gaussian KDE unfolding of eigenvalues   bandwidth        = "nrd0",            # KDE bandwidth rule (stats::density default)   nr.fit.points    = 20,                # support points (only used if unfold.method = "spline")   discard.outliers = TRUE,              # IQR-trim extreme eigenvalues before unfolding   discard.zeros    = TRUE,              # drop all-zero rows/cols after thresholding   min.mat.dim      = 40,                # early-stop if effective dim drops below 40   max.ev.spacing   = 3,                 # truncate NNSD tail at spacing = 3   save_plots       = FALSE,             # don't write diagnostic PNGs to disk   out_dir          = "RMT_plots",       # (only used when save_plots = TRUE)   verbose          = TRUE,              # print scan progress to console   seed             = 1115               # fix RNG for reproducibility )  # The chosen threshold to feed downstream into build_graph_from_mat(r.threshold = ...) out$chosen_threshold

what: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: Aggregates two adjacency matrices – typically produced different network inference methods (e.g. SparCC, SpiecEasi, WGCNA, Hmisc, plain correlation) set features – single consensus network returns `tbl_graph` consistent rest `build_graph_from_*()` family. Combining multiple methods standard strategy reducing method-specific bias biological network inference; see Aghayeva et al. (2024, CMiNet) Chowdhury et al. (2024, hybrid Bayesian / ML / network framework) related approaches.

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
code: build_graph_from_consensus(   adj_list,   method = c("rank_fusion", "intersection", "weighted_average", "majority_vote"),   rank_fusion_algorithm = c("borda", "rra", "rrf"),   threshold = NULL,   binarize = c("none", "threshold", "topk"),   binarize_threshold = 0,   binarize_topk = NULL,   weights = NULL,   min_methods = NULL,   rrf_k = 60,   node_handling = c("intersect", "union"),   module.method = c("Fast_greedy", "Walktrap", "Edge_betweenness", "Spinglass"),   node_annotation = NULL,   top_modules = 15,   seed = 1115 )

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: adj_list Named unnamed list least two square numeric adjacency matrices. matrices must row column names identifying features; matrices need share identical feature sets (see `node_handling`). Pre-thresholded inputs (zeros non-significant pairs) supported recommended. method Character. Top-level consensus strategy. One `"rank_fusion"` (default), `"intersection"`, `"weighted_average"`, `"majority_vote"`. See Method details. rank_fusion_algorithm Character. used `method = "rank_fusion"`. One `"borda"` (default), `"rra"`, `"rrf"`. See Rank fusion algorithms. threshold Numeric `NULL` (default). Optional final absolute-weight cutoff applied consensus matrix; entries `abs(w) < threshold` zeroed . binarize Character. used `"intersection"` `"majority_vote"`. One `"none"` (default; treat non-zero entry edge), `"threshold"` (apply `binarize_threshold`), `"topk"` (keep global top-`binarize_topk` strongest edges per matrix). binarize_threshold Numeric (default `0`). Per-method `|w| >= binarize_threshold` edge cut-`binarize = "threshold"`. binarize_topk Integer `NULL`. Per-method top-K cut-`binarize = "topk"`. weights Numeric vector `NULL` (default). Per-method weights `"weighted_average"`. Length must match `length( adj_list)`; values renormalised sum 1. `NULL` uses uniform weights. min_methods Integer `NULL` (default). Minimum number methods must support edge `"majority_vote"`. `NULL` defaults strict majority (`floor(M/2) + 1` `M` number methods). rrf_k Numeric (default `60`). Smoothing constant reciprocal rank fusion (`method = "rank_fusion", rank_fusion_algorithm = "rrf"`). node_handling Character. align features present every input matrix. `"intersect"` (default) keeps features common inputs; `"union"` keeps every feature appearing input treats missing entries zero. module.method Character. Module detection method passed [build_graph_from_adj_mat()] constructing final `tbl_graph`. One `"Fast_greedy"`, `"Walktrap"`, `"Edge_betweenness"`, `"Spinglass"`. node_annotation Optional data frame attached vertex metadata; first column must match feature names consensus matrix. top_modules Integer (default `15`). Number top-ranked modules retain final `tbl_graph`; smaller modules collapsed `"Others"`. seed Integer (default `1115`). Random seed.

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: `tbl_graph` object whose schema matches rest   `build_graph_from_*()` family (vertex columns `name`,   `modularity`, `modularity2`, `modularity3`, `Modularity`,   `Degree`, `Strength`; edge columns `weight`, `correlation`,   `corr_direction`). Plug straight [ggNetView()]   visualisation.

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: Four consensus strategies supported `method`. Three (`"intersection"`, `"weighted_average"`, `"majority_vote"`) operate directly input weights; fourth (`"rank_fusion"`) converts method's adjacency ranks first, makes aggregation invariant different weight scales produced different inference algorithms (correlation [-1, 1], partial correlation, TOM [0, 1], ...). `method = "rank_fusion"`, three classical rank-aggregation algorithms available via `rank_fusion_algorithm`: Borda count (mean rank), Robust Rank Aggregation (RRA, Kolde et al. 2012), Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, Cormack et al. 2009).

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: `"intersection"` edge survives consensus iff     non-zero (`binarize`) **every** input matrix.     Consensus weight mean input weights surviving     edges. Strictest four strategies. `"weighted_average"` input matrix min-max     normalised [0, 1] absolute value (sign preserved),     combined weighted sum using `weights` (default uniform).     Consensus weight [-1, 1] inherits sign     methods dominate average. `"majority_vote"` input matrix binarised, edges     summed, edge survives consensus iff count     least `min_methods`. Consensus weight mean     input weights restricted methods voted yes. `"rank_fusion"` input matrix's pairs ranked     `|w|` (descending). Ranks aggregated according     `rank_fusion_algorithm`, min-max normalised [-1, 1]     (sign taken mean input weights). robust     across-method scale differences.

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: `"borda"` Mean rank across methods. Lower mean rank =     supported edge. Simple, assumptions, good baseline. `"rra"` Robust Rank Aggregation (Kolde et al. 2012,     Bioinformatics). Computes rho-score pair     null hypothesis uniformly distributed ranks; edges     small rho consistently outrank random expectation. Uses     `RobustRankAggreg` package available; otherwise falls back     inline Beta-order-statistic implementation. Output score     `-log10(rho)` larger = confident. `"rrf"` Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al. 2009).     Per-edge score `sum_m 1 / (k + rank_m)` `k = rrf_k`     (default 60, information-retrieval convention). Robust     extreme rank values, parameter tuning required.

title: Build a consensus graph object from multiple adjacency matrices — build_graph_from_consensus
text: Kolde, R., Laur, S., Adler, P., & Vilo, J. (2012). Robust rank aggregation gene list integration meta-analysis. *Bioinformatics*, 28(4), 573-580. Cormack, G. V., Clarke, C. L. ., & Buettcher, S. (2009). Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms Condorcet individual rank learning methods. *Proceedings 32nd International ACM SIGIR Conference*, 758-759. Aghayeva, R., et al. (2024). CMiNet: R package user-friendly Shiny App constructing consensus microbiome networks. Chowdhury, S., et al. (2024). hybrid framework disease biomarker discovery microbiome research combining Bayesian networks, machine learning, network-based methods.

Options include: "none" (raw data), "scale" (z-score standardization), "center" (mean centering ), "log2" (log2 transfrom), "log10" (log10 transfrom), "ln" (natural transfrom ), "rrarefy" (random rarefaction using vegan::rrarefy), "rrarefy_relative" (rarefy convert relative abundance). r.threshold Numeric. Options include "pearson", "kendall", "spearman". proc Character. Correlation p-value adjustment methods. Options include: "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH", "", "fdr", "none". module.method Character. Network community detection (module identification) method. Options include "Fast_greedy", "Walktrap", "Edge_betweenness", "Spinglass". SpiecEasi.method Character. Method used SpiecEasi network inference; options include "mb" "glasso". sparcc_R Integer. title: Build a graph object from a STRING database export — build_graph_from_stringdb
text: stringdb Either file path (`.tsv` / `.tsv.gz`) data.frame already loaded memory. STRING-style headers (leading `#` first column name) handled automatically. node1_col, node2_col, score_col Character. Column names use edge ``, ``, weight columns. Defaults match STRING's TSV layout (`"node1"`, `"node2"`, `"combined_score"`). Override want weight individual evidence channel – e.g. `score_col = "experimentally_determined_interaction"`. score_threshold Numeric `NULL` (default). non-NULL, edges `score_col < score_threshold` dropped. STRING confidence cut-offs typically `0.4` (medium), `0.7` (high), `0.9` (highest). Pass `NULL` keep every edge input. node_annotation Optional data frame; first column must match protein/gene names appearing `node1_col` / `node2_col`. provided, annotations attached vertex attributes via [build_graph_from_df()]. directed Logical (default: `FALSE`). STRING interactions undirected convention. module.method Character. Network community detection method. Options: `"Fast_greedy"`, `"Walktrap"`, `"Edge_betweenness"`, `"Spinglass"`. top_modules Integer. Number top-ranked modules retain; smaller modules collapsed `"Others"`. seed Integer (default: `1115`). Random seed reproducibility.

title: Compute the Integrated Value of Influence (IVI) per node — get_node_ivi
text: Computes Integrated Value Influence (IVI) Salavaty et al. (2020) attaches per-node score new vertex column input `tbl_graph`. IVI integrates six centrality measures across three levels – local (degree, local H-index), semi-local (ClusterRank), global (betweenness, closeness, collective influence) – robust single centrality identifying influential nodes complex biological networks (microbiome co-occurrence, gene co-expression, PPI, ...).

code: get_node_ivi(   graph_obj,   weights = NULL,   mode = c("all", "in", "out"),   directed = FALSE,   d = 3,   scale = c("range", "z-scale", "none"),   ncores = 1L,   overwrite = TRUE )

title: Compute the Integrated Value of Influence (IVI) per node — get_node_ivi
text: graph_obj `tbl_graph` produced `build_graph_from_*()` constructor. weights Numeric vector `NULL` (default). Edge weights pass `influential::ivi()`. `NULL` uses unweighted IVI definition. Pass string `"weight"` use graph's existing `weight` edge attribute IVI weights (interpreted distances `influential::ivi`). mode Character (default `""`). Edge mode passed `influential::ivi()`. One `""`, `""`, `""`. `""` right choice undirected graphs. directed Logical (default `FALSE`). Whether graph treated directed. Passed `influential::ivi()`. d Integer (default `3`). Distance horizon used collective-influence component. Larger `d` looks farther node scoring increases run-time roughly linearly. IVI paper recommends `d = 3` good trade-. scale Character (default `"range"`). scale IVI values returned `influential::ivi()`: `"range"` Normalise `[1, 100]`. Use     exploring single network; lets see full spread     node influences. `"z-scale"` z-score standardisation. Use     comparing IVI across multiple networks, want     defensible numeric threshold (`z > 1.645` common cutoff     "significantly influential"). `"none"` Return raw IVI scores scaling. older versions `influential` exposed boolean `scaled` argument instead `scale`, wrapper automatically translates: `"none"` -> `scaled = FALSE`, anything else -> `scaled = TRUE`. ncores Integer (default `1`). Number parallel cores `influential::ivi()`'s internal cluster-rank step. default (`1`) forces serial execution – deliberately conservative wrapper works inside `R CMD check` (caps tests 2 cores via `_R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_`) inside vignette builds (leftover parallel clusters common source "9 simultaneous processes spawned" / "invalid connection" errors). interactive production work real network, raising e.g. `4` `parallel::detectCores() - 1` gives meaningful speed-. overwrite Logical (default `TRUE`). `IVI` column already exists input graph, controls whether overwrite (silent overwrite `TRUE`; warning + return unchanged `FALSE`).

title: Compute the Integrated Value of Influence (IVI) per node — get_node_ivi
text: Different `influential` releases exposed slightly different argument lists `ivi()`. Recent releases (one package developed ) accept `scale` string values `"range"` / `"z-scale"` / `"none"`; older releases used `scaled` logical instead. stay forward- backward-compatible, wrapper inspects `formals(influential::ivi)` call time translates user-facing `scale` argument whichever signature installed version expects. Arguments installed version recognise silently dropped call.

Controls tightly nodes fill module's allocated disc WGCNA bubble-pack layout: 1 (default) nodes spread fill 95 percent disc (original behaviour); smaller values (e.g. 0.65) contract FR/uniform fill toward module centre, exposing hub/periphery structure producing visible inter-module whitespace. Build per-sample module summary matrix spec_df shape     (samples x modules) using either module_eigengene (PC1     module's OTU sub-matrix; recommended) module_abundance     (sum / mean OTU abundances inside module). (env_block, modules) pair, compute either     correlation Mantel test (see Mantel API ). Render network via ggNetView (parameters     forwarded ...), draw four heatmap quadrants env-env     correlations, overlay link segments module anchors env     diagonals. Mantel API (shared gglink_heatmaps). Two algorithms exposed via mantel_kind; go helpers mantel_block_vs_col / mantel_pairwise two top-level functions stay numerically identical: "block_vs_col" (default, ecological standard):     module, OTUs belong pulled otu_mat     (transposed samples x OTUs) turned ONE community     distance matrix spec_dist_method; env column     turned distance matrix env_dist_method;     one Mantel test per (module, env_col). "col_vs_col" (legacy): module's representative vector     (eigengene abundance) treated single variable;     single-column distance matrix tested env column's     single-column distance matrix. Mathematically close rank     correlation. Kept backwards compatibility / sensitivity     comparisons. Prior versions function used equivalent "col_vs_col" implicitly. default switched "block_vs_col" (one-time message() first Mantel call) match standard ecological interpretation; pass mantel_kind = "col_vs_col" reproduce old numbers. Output schema stable across modes. returned stats data frame always columns ID, Type, Correlation, Pvalue, p_signif, spec_block, env_block, method. Full-panel styling is passed through via `full_args`. full_style <- list(   layout_module   = "adjacent",  # neighbouring modules close together   node_size_range = c(1, 5),     # node size range   center        = FALSE,       # do not pull nodes to module centre   shrink        = 0.9,         # compact layout   edge_alpha    = 0.2,         # edge transparency   edge_color    = "#d9d9d9"    # edge colour ) ggnetview_subgraph(obj, select_module = "1", full_args = full_style)  # Outline modules via ggNetView's own module_outline, on BOTH panels. ggnetview_subgraph(   obj, select_module = "1",   full_args = c(full_style, list(module_outline = TRUE)),   sub_args  = list(module_outline = TRUE) )  # Re-lay-out the subgraph as a clean circle, recoloured teal. ggnetview_subgraph(   obj,   select_module = "1",   sub_layout    = "circle",   sub_fill      = "#2C7C82",   full_args     = full_style )  # Select THREE modules and lay the subgraph out as a tripartite network. ggnetview_subgraph(   obj,   select_module = c("1", "2", "3"),   sub_layout    = "tripartite_gephi_layout",   full_args     = full_style ) } # }

text: nodes_bulk Data frame tibble. Node table modularity degree information. Node IDs must rownames name column (compatible tidygraph::as_tibble output). z_bulk_mat Numeric matrix. Adjacency correlation matrix; rows columns must correspond nodes. Non-zero entries treated edges. NA/Inf replaced 0. modularity_col Character. Column name nodes_bulk containing module labels. degree_col Character. Column name nodes_bulk containing node degree (number edges). Note: column validated (must exist free NA). participation coefficient (Pi) derives node's total degree z_bulk_mat directly, values degree_col enter Zi/Pi computation. zi_threshold Numeric (default = 2.5). Threshold within-module connectivity (Zi) role classification. pi_threshold Numeric (default = 0.62). Threshold among-module connectivity (Pi) role classification. na.rm Logical (default = FALSE). TRUE, remove rows NA Zi Pi output. FALSE, keep rows; NA Zi/Pi results type = NA. point_colors Named character vector (NULL). Point/legend colours four node roles. Defaults c("Peripherals" = "#377eb8", "Connectors" = "#4daf4a", "Module hubs" = "#e41a1c", "Network hubs" = "#ff7f00"). may override four, subset (role name), pass single colour apply every role. bg_colors Named character vector (NULL). Colours four quadrant text labels, keyed role. Defaults black four. override rules point_colors. label_size Numeric (default = 5.5). Text size four quadrant labels. bg_alpha Numeric (default = 0.25). Opacity quadrant background shading (0 = transparent, 1 = opaque).

title: Compute Zi-Pi (within-module connectivity and participation coefficient) — ggnetview_zipi
text: Zi (within-module connectivity): Reflects strongly node connected within module. Higher values indicate node connections within module may play core role inside . Pi (among-module connectivity): Measures much node connects modules. Higher values indicate node acts bridge modules, facilitating information, material energy flow across network. Node roles (default thresholds Zi=2.5, Pi=0.62): Module hubs: High Zi, low Pi. Core members within module,     important module stability function, weakly connected     modules. Connectors: Low Zi, high Pi. prominent within module,     strongly connect across modules, acting bridges. Network hubs: High Zi, high Pi. Core nodes within     across modules, critical overall network structure stability. Peripherals: Low Zi, low Pi. Peripheral satellite nodes     connections within across modules.

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
text: Approximates classic ecological *press perturbation*: treats signed correlation matrix proxy community (interaction) matrix \(\), adds negative self-regulation diagonal, inverts obtain net-effect matrix \(N = -^{-1}\). Entry \(N_{ij}\) long-run net response node \(\) node \(j\) held sustained pressure (continuously elevated suppressed). closest one can get "type 3" dynamical perturbation static correlation network.

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
code: press_perturbation(   graph_obj = NULL,   cor_mat = NULL,   self_regulation = NULL,   source = NULL )

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
text: graph_obj `tbl_graph` `build_graph_from_*()` constructor. Ignored `cor_mat` supplied. cor_mat Optional numeric matrix. signed correlation / interaction matrix matching row/col names, used directly instead extracting one `graph_obj`. self_regulation Numeric scalar, `NULL` (default). diagonal `` (intraspecific density dependence; must negative). `NULL`, set automatically `-(max Re eigenvalue(-diagonal ) + 1)`, guarantees stable matrix. Supply (e.g. `-1`) encode specific assumption. source Optional character vector node `name`s. given, `response` returns net effect every node pressing source node(s).

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
text: list : `net_effect`: \(N = -^{-1}\) matrix (columns = pressed       node, rows = responding node). `stable`: logical; `TRUE` `` dynamically stable. `eigen_real_max`: largest real part ``'s eigenvalues       (must `< 0` stability). `self_regulation`: diagonal value actually used. `response`: `source` given, data frame net       response node pressing source(s); else `NULL`.

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
text: deliberately approximate, *qualitative* method. Correlation **** causation carries direction, interaction signs magnitudes proxies, measured coefficients. framework also requires community matrix **dynamically stable** (eigenvalues `` negative real part); `press_perturbation()` checks warns fails. Treat output defensible qualitative scenario ("keep suppressing taxon , community tends shift way"), never quantitative prediction. purely structural read stability assumption, use [get_network_perturbation()] [get_node_influence()].

title: Press-perturbation (sustained-disturbance) analysis — press_perturbation
text: Bender EA, Case TJ, Gilpin (1984). "Perturbation experiments community ecology: theory practice." Ecology 65(1):1-13. May RM (1972). "large complex system stable?" Nature 238:413-414. Novak M et al. (2016). "Characterizing species interactions understand press perturbations." Annu. Rev. Ecol. Evol. Syst. 47:409-432.

title: ggNetView 0.1.0
text: Initial submission ggNetView CRAN. Provides unified, reproducible framework analyzing visualizing complex biological, ecological, microbial association networks. Includes tools building correlation co-occurrence networks via WGCNA, SpiecEasi, SparCC, standard correlation methods (Pearson, Spearman, Kendall). Computes node-level network-level topological metrics, including robustness analyses. Supports module-level analyses (modularity detection, Zi-Pi classification, sample-level subgraph topology). Offers large family deterministic layout generators built ggraph ggplot2 (bipartite, tripartite, quadripartite, pentapartite, circular-modules, petal, diamond, heart, star, ), reproducible seeds. Ships 18 example datasets covering OTU tables, taxonomy tables, environmental metadata, PPI networks, modularity examples.
